input:
the two lifetime values reported for the benchmark material differ by more than either group's stated repeatability, and the difference sits in the test conditions rather than in the material. One group ages its samples under continuous flow and reports the time at which uptake has fallen to a stated fraction of the fresh value, while the other ages under repeated cycling and reports the cycle count at which the same fraction is reached. A lifetime stated in hours and a lifetime stated in cycles are not two measurements of one quantity until the duty is matched, and the flow group's figure can only be converted to the cycling group's basis on an assumed cycle length that neither group states.
IAST enters the comparison because both groups correct their working capacities with it, and the correction is larger for the group whose feed carries the heavier contaminant load. On matched duty — the same contaminant load, the same regeneration, and the end of life taken at the same retained fraction — the cycling group's value is the one this review rests on, because its samples met the contaminant in the form the application carries. The preference holds only on that condition: on a continuous duty with the lighter contaminant load, the flow group's value is the applicable one, and the lifetime in service will be set by the duty the application imposes.
